items.reasoning: Let l be the old left dimension, O=Fin 2 x Fin r, e:O~Fin(2r), and k=min(l,2r). The flat matrix is Af(a,j)=A(a,e^-1(j)). The row Gram entry is sum_o Qf(a,e(o))Qf(c,e(o)), equal by bijective finite reindexing to the flat Gram delta(a,c). These calculations independently justify all three rubric requirements and the reference answer, including the exact dimension k. The word inverse is harmless here: transporting the flat labeling back means precomposing with e on an original pair. The full exists_core_lq body does exactly these two calculations, and I inspected the complete ThinLQ existence proof rather than assuming the name implies a factorization. k is a thin ambient dimension, not necessarily the matrix rank: rank-deficient and zero matrices are included. If l=0 or r=0 then k=0 and the empty products and identities have the correct carriers. This is conditional on a thin orthonormal factorization/existence theorem, not a constructive efficiency claim. Nearby la-012 asks consequences of an already given backward min recurrence; sp-004 asks global boundary mass, and la-206/la-218 ask stored-operation cost/dispatch contracts. None requests this bijection/product/Gram transport conclusion, so the bounded candidates are not exact aliases.

items.reasoning: All five recursive evaluation equations are correct, and evaluation is surjective because rat(q) maps to every rational q. The source, however, defines Coeff as raw inductive expression syntax with constructors rat, symbol, add, mul and neg and structural DecidableEq. It supplies constructor operations, not a quotient by ring identities. For example add(rat(0),rat(0)) is a different constructor term from rat(0), so zero+zero=zero is false as an equality of Coeff; associatively rebracketed add trees are likewise distinct. Thus this carrier with those source operations is not a ring or a rational algebra in the ordinary ring/algebra sense. The reference answer's unqualified homomorphism-of-the-symbolic-coefficient-algebra claim, and especially rubric r3 demanding a '(ring/algebra) homomorphism', conceal this distinction precisely where the question asks for the structure to be stated accurately. A correct weaker statement is that evalWith is a surjective homomorphism for the operation signature, i.e. an interpretation of the free term algebra, preserving the displayed constructors and constants. One may also descend to a suitably specified quotient algebra, but neither that quotient nor its well-definedness is in the record or source. If 'algebra' were explicitly defined in the universal-algebra sense, the constructor-preservation assertion would be sound; the current rubric does not make that qualification and allows the false ring-homomorphism identification as gold. I therefore reject this exact answer/rubric record rather than silently supply the missing interpretation. This is an exposition/category mismatch, not a failure of the source evalWith equations. Within the bounded candidate set, no other task asks about this symbolic evaluation object; its semantic core is distinct independently of this correctness finding.

items.reasoning: For V:N x r real, (V^T V)(a,b)=sum_i V(i,a)V(i,b)=delta(a,b), so its columns are orthonormal. Taking inner products with the columns in any vanishing linear combination forces each coefficient zero and gives r<=N. An injection e:Fin r -> Fin N identifies r distinct physical positions; the partial family f(e(a))=V_col(a) is well-defined because e is injective and stays orthonormal. Finite-dimensional orthonormal-basis extension fills the complement of image(e), which has N-r labels; placing that full basis in columns produces U^T U=I and U(i,e(a))=V(i,a). This accounts for every ingredient requested by the question and every rubric step, including arbitrary noncontiguous placement. I read the complete proof: it forms the range-restricted family, applies orthonormal-basis extension with dimension N, and extracts the two required entrywise conclusions. r=0 is completion of the empty family; r=N leaves no freedom and yields the prescribed frame with its assigned order; N=r=0 yields the empty orthogonal matrix. Neither determinant +1 nor a computational Gram-Schmidt implementation or preprocessing cost follows, and the answer promises only existence. la-006 adds a spare-column orientation constraint, la-009 extracts the dimension/counting obstruction, and la-011 asks for a full-frame counterexample. Those statements have shared ingredients but are not identical to arbitrary-position orthogonal completion.

items.reasoning: Taking determinants of U^T U=I gives det(U)^2=1 over the reals. If det(U)=1 keep U. Otherwise pick j outside image(e), which exists since r<N, and take S diagonal with S(j,j)=-1 and every other diagonal entry +1. Then S^T S=I, det(S)=-1, (US)^T(US)=I and det(US)=1. The entry formula (US)(i,k)=U(i,k)S(k,k) proves exactly that only column j changes sign. In particular every prescribed column e(a) is unchanged, with no sign or global-phase weakening of its entries. The complete signFlip lemmas and both special-orthogonal completion proofs use the same argument, and the answer/rubric correctly distinguish right multiplication from row flipping. Strictness guarantees N>0 and an available column; it is sufficient for every data set, not necessary for an individual already positively oriented full frame. The question and answer say 'cannot in general' when r=N, which is correct: for N>=1 a fully prescribed reflection is an obstruction, while an already positive full frame and the N=0 empty frame need no repair. There is no claimed search cost for the unused label or efficient completion algorithm. la-011 overlaps the last obstruction explanation, but its entire task is the boundary counterexample; la-006 additionally requires a universal constructive orientation repair for all strict frames. la-005 only guarantees O(N), and la-009 only dimension/counting. items.reasoning: For any finite complex A:m x n and scalars a,b, mulVec additivity and complex scalar homogeneity give A(a e_left+b e_right)=a A e_left+b A e_right. Each basis delta kills every term of the finite input sum except its named column, so the result is a col_left(A)+b col_right(A), and output coordinate k is a A(k,left)+b A(k,right). No conjugation of a or b appears: this is a linear operator action, not an inner product. The complete source definitions and both vector/coordinate proofs match this derivation, and all four rubric criteria are satisfied. The indices need not be different; if left=right the amplitudes combine to (a+b) times one column. Either coefficient may be zero; no normalization, orthogonality, square shape or unitarity is required. A zero input dimension admits no chosen basis indices, while an empty output carrier gives the empty-vector equality. The practical 'only two columns/entries' consequence is valid for the stated two-term input or that one queried output amplitude. It must not be read as saying arbitrary dense inputs or full all-input block-encoding verification need only two columns; nor does it bound the cost of retrieving either column. The answer itself scopes the sufficiency statement to a two-term superposition. la-008 asks a universal clean-branch certificate equivalence over every basis pair, and la-004 is register reindexing; neither is an exact alias of sparse two-term linearity.
